shadows.name: panel-chrome

shadows.name: button-primary-chrome
shadows.purpose: Bright inset top edge plus a short amber-tinted cast so the primary action sits proud.

shadows.name: led-emission
shadows.purpose: Not a box-shadow. A radial-gradient halo layered behind LEDs and lit jacks — the only way the world emits light.

shadows.name: pulse-ignite
shadows.purpose: Filter on the active cable's travelling signal pulse; brightness, not element glow.

motion.name: pointer-spring
motion.purpose: Spring smoothing on the shared cursor-reactive pointer so cables follow and settle, never snap.

motion.name: signal-dash
motion.purpose: The one continuous travelling pulse on the active patch cable.

motion.name: led-breathe
motion.purpose: Ambient jack and status LED breathing.

motion.name: knob-sway
motion.purpose: Optional ambient knob-indicator sway around its set value.

motion.name: reduced-motion-guard
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) flattens all animation/transition durations to 0.01ms
motion.purpose: The world is fully reduced-motion-safe; cables drop cursor-follow and dash.

narrative.overview: The portfolio is a modular signal rack sitting in a dark studio room. Every surface is a brushed-aluminium front panel bolted into a rack: silkscreen legends, engraved seams, rack-ear screws, jacks, knobs, VU meters, and rubber patch cables carrying signal from input to output. The work is not described as a system — it is shown as one, hardware a visitor can trace signal through. The mood is engineered, tactile, and quietly powered-on. Depth is physical — every panel reads as a milled metal face catching a single top light, never a floating card with a drop shadow. Color is almost entirely neutral graphite and bone; the signal-amber accent is rationed so that when it appears it reads as live current, not decoration. Motion is the physics of real hardware: damped springs that settle rather than snap, one continuous signal pulse on the active patch, and ambient life from breathing jack LEDs and drifting VU needles. The default and canonical theme is dark; a light theme exists and re-derives every token, but the dark palette is the source of truth.
keyCharacteristics: Brushed-metal panels with engraved seams and inset bevels — never flat floating cards.
Silkscreen mono legends and instrument readouts label everything, like a real rack.
One rationed signal color (amber) marks what is live; patch-cyan is the resting signal.
Hardware primitives (jacks, knobs, VU meters, patch cables) stand in for stock UI.
Motion settles like real analog parts; emission is radial-gradient light, never box-shadow glow.

rules.name: The Live-Current Rule
rules.body: Amber marks only what is live: the primary action, a lit jack, the active cable, an ignited module. If more than a small fraction of a view is amber, something inert has been wrongly energized. Everything at rest is graphite, bone, and — for dormant signal — cyan.

rules.name: The Channel-Native Color Rule
rules.body: Values are authored as space-separated RGB channels in CSS variables (--c-accent: 242 163 60) so Tailwind opacity modifiers compose. Consume colors through the semantic tokens, never as raw hex in components.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Instrumentation Rule
rules.body: Chivo Mono is for machine-labeling only: silkscreen legends, readouts, levels, coordinates, timestamps, button and nav labels. It never sets prose.

rules.name: The Legible-Floor Rule
rules.body: Functional text never drops below 11px. Silk labels and chips sit at the 0.7rem (11.2px) floor; nothing smaller ships.

rules.name: The Emission-Not-Glow Rule
rules.body: LEDs, lit jacks, and active emphasis emit light via a radial-gradient halo layered behind the element, never a box-shadow glow. Box-shadow is reserved for structural bevels and contact shadows; signal brightness on the active cable comes from a drop-shadow filter on the pulse stroke.

rules.name: The Milled-Face Rule
rules.body: Every container is a milled panel: 1px line border, 8px radius, inset bevel. Surfaces are never borderless floating cards and never carry a soft ambient drop shadow as their resting state.

dos: Do build every container as a milled panel: 1px line seam, 8px radius, inset bevel; reach for .panel / .panel-raised.
Do ration amber to live current — the primary action, lit jacks, the active cable, an ignited module (The Live-Current Rule).
Do label hardware with mono silk legends and readouts; keep Archivo for prose (The Mono-Is-Instrumentation Rule).
Do emit light with radial-gradient halos and pulse drop-shadows; keep box-shadow for bevels and contact shadows (The Emission-Not-Glow Rule).
Do let moving parts settle with spring physics, and guard every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion.
Do keep chrome integer-aligned and functional text at or above 11px (The Legible-Floor Rule).
Do use patch-cyan for dormant signal and amber for the ignited/active state.
donts: Don't render stock floating cards or buttons with soft ambient drop shadows — the material is milled metal, not paper.
Don't spread amber across inert chrome; if most of a view is amber, something inert was wrongly energized.
Don't set prose or headings in Chivo Mono, and don't label hardware in Archivo.
Don't fake LED or active glow with box-shadow; use a radial-gradient emission layer.
Don't let any moving part snap; and never ship motion that ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't drop functional text below 11px or let panel chrome fall off integer pixel alignment.
